title: Credibility of the measures to enhance the career perspectives and employability of the researcher and contribution to his/her skills development
content:
## 2.1 Credibility of the measures to enhance the career perspectives and employability of the researcher and contribution to his/her skills development

### Starting point and career target

FIELDWISE is a 30-month MSCA European Fellowship structured as a 24-month European Fellowship at HUN-REN ATK followed by a six-month non-academic placement at AgroVIR. The recruited researcher, Dr. Rositsa Cholakova, enters the fellowship as an accomplished plant physiologist and agronomist: a BSc/MSc in Plant Protection/Agronomy, a PhD in Plant Physiology, approximately five years of university teaching and research in plant stress physiology, and an expanding technical profile in remote sensing, hyperspectral sensing, UAV applications, GIS and agricultural data analysis. The measures below are not generic training add-ons; they are designed around one explicit, evidence-based career objective. The fellowship addresses the single remaining competence gap in this profile — rigorous predictive modelling and model validation across time, sensing scales and environments — and thereby completes the researcher's progression from a plant physiologist/agronomist who uses digital tools into an independent Agricultural Data Scientist specialised in plant stress, Earth observation and decision-support systems. Every measure is chosen to close a named part of that gap, so that the enhancement of career perspectives is specific and demonstrable rather than asserted.

### Specific measures to enhance career perspectives and employability

**A jointly owned Career Development Plan.** The backbone of the career-development effort is a Career Development Plan, established jointly by the supervisors and the researcher and delivered as an early project deliverable (D1.3 Career Development Plan, due M3). The plan links the four research objectives to concrete training and career needs, a transferable-skills programme, a teaching route, publication planning and open-science engagement, and it is not a one-off document: it is revisited at several defined review points spread across the action, including a mid-placement review, so that training investment is monitored and adjusted against the researcher's evolving career goals. This gives the fellowship an auditable mechanism for steering skills acquisition toward employability rather than leaving development to chance.

**Interdisciplinary, supervised two-way transfer of knowledge.** The scientific training is delivered as supervised practice in a genuinely interdisciplinary environment. Primary supervision at HUN-REN ATK is provided by Dr. Roland Hollós, who anchors training in heterogeneous agricultural-data integration, AI/ML-supported modelling, feature engineering, validation design, uncertainty analysis and model interpretation; his standing as a HUN-REN AI Ambassador connects the fellow to a network-wide AI-for-Science environment. Co-supervision at the associated partner Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) is provided by Prof. András Jung, who carries the geoinformatics, field-spectroscopy, hyperspectral/UAV and scale-aware Earth-observation training strand. The transfer is deliberately two-way and complementary: the fellow brings agronomy, plant physiology, plant-stress biology, physiological phenotyping and proximal spectral interpretation into the modelling and remote-sensing environment, and receives in return the data-science, robust-modelling and multi-sensor integration competences her profile currently lacks. This international and interdisciplinary configuration is the core mechanism by which the fellowship forges new mind-sets and approaches to research and innovation work.

**A structured transferable-skills portfolio.** Alongside the scientific training, the Career Development Plan commits the fellow to a defined transferable-skills programme covering research integrity, open science and FAIR practice, generative-AI literacy, grant writing, IP and exploitation, project management and science communication. These are the competences that convert scientific results into an independent research career: grant writing and project management underpin the transition toward principal-investigator roles; IP, exploitation and open-science literacy support both academic and industry pathways; and generative-AI literacy is directly relevant to the data-science identity the fellowship is building.

**An inter-sectoral non-academic placement.** Employability outside academia is addressed directly through a six-month non-academic placement at AgroVIR in the final phase of the action. The placement supplies competences the academic host cannot provide alone: operational model evaluation, research-to-MVP translation, agricultural-software requirements engineering, interoperability assessment, user-centred decision support and exploitation planning. It is supervised by Miklós Maróti, Managing Director of AgroVIR, and is conducted mainly through remote collaboration with monthly face-to-face technical meetings. Because AgroVIR is additionally consulted from the start of the action, the placement deepens an established collaboration rather than opening a cold one, and the fellow arrives at it already familiar with the industrial partner's needs. This inter-sectoral exposure is precisely the kind of career move between sectors and organisations that the call promotes as a driver of expanded career opportunities and knowledge transfer.

**A teaching and dissemination route.** The fellowship also protects and extends the researcher's teaching capability. As HUN-REN ATK is a research organisation rather than a university, the teaching route runs through short guest lectures, seminars and practical sessions at MATE and, where institutionally possible, the Agricultural University of Plovdiv (AU Plovdiv), transferring the fellow's approximately five years of university teaching in Plant Physiology and Plant Stress Physiology (2015-2020, including syllabus design, lecturing and examining in Bulgarian and English, and Bachelor's supervision) into the new discipline of agricultural data science. Scientific dissemination targets at least two high-quality peer-reviewed publications, with a possible third methods/application paper, giving the fellow a visible independent publication record from the action.

### Expected contribution of the skills development to the future career

Taken together, these measures produce a distinctive and marketable competence profile. By completion, the fellow will have carried a scientific concept through biological definition, model development, unseen-condition validation, software implementation and industrial evaluation — an end-to-end trajectory that few early-career agricultural data scientists can evidence. This profile is deliberately dual-track. Within academia it qualifies the researcher for independent, grant-winning positions at universities, European research organisations, crop-phenotyping groups and Earth-observation/geospatial research units, supported by the modelling, validation, grant-writing and publication competences acquired. Beyond academia it opens roles in precision-agriculture and irrigation-technology companies, farm-management information system (FMIS) providers and geospatial-service organisations, supported by the requirements-engineering, interoperability, exploitation-planning and user-centred design experience gained on the AgroVIR placement. The combination of a physiological and agronomic foundation with rigorous data-science and inter-sectoral experience is difficult to acquire on either an academic or an industrial track alone, and it is exactly this combination that FIELDWISE is engineered to deliver.

These career and skills measures address the call's expected outcomes and impacts directly: they deliver an increased set of research and transferable skills and competences leading to improved employability and career prospects within academia and beyond (EO-01/EI-01); they forge new mind-sets and approaches to research and innovation work through international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary experience (EO-02); and, through the non-academic placement, they stimulate knowledge transfer and expand career opportunities via a career move between sectors (EI-02). The credibility of the plan rests on the fact that each measure is tied to a named competence gap, is owned and monitored through a jointly agreed and periodically reviewed Career Development Plan, and is delivered within a supervision and partner configuration that already exists around the researcher.

claim_statuses.claim_summary: FIELDWISE is a 30-month MSCA European Fellowship comprising a 24-month European Fellowship at HUN-REN ATK plus a six-month non-academic placement at AgroVIR.
The host and recruiting organisation is HUN-REN ATK and the primary supervisor is Dr. Roland Hollós.
The co-supervisor is Prof. András Jung at the associated partner Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE).

The fellow Dr. Rositsa Cholakova is a plant physiologist/agronomist (BSc/MSc Plant Protection/Agronomy, PhD Plant Physiology, ~5 years university teaching) with an expanding technical profile in remote sensing, hyperspectral sensing, UAV, GIS and agricultural data analysis.

The fellowship closes the remaining competence gap in predictive modelling and validation, completing the researcher's progression to an independent Agricultural Data Scientist specialised in plant stress, Earth observation and decision support.
A Career Development Plan (deliverable D1.3, due M3) is established jointly by supervisors and researcher and reviewed at several defined points across the action, including a mid-placement review.

Structured transferable-skills training covers research integrity, open science and FAIR practice, generative-AI literacy, grant writing, IP and exploitation, project management and science communication.

The fellowship provides an interdisciplinary two-way transfer of knowledge in which the fellow acquires agricultural data science, robust modelling, uncertainty analysis and hyperspectral/UAV/EO integration while contributing agronomy, plant physiology and proximal spectral interpretation.
Dr. Roland Hollós is a HUN-REN AI Ambassador, linking the training to a network-wide AI-for-Science environment.
Dr. Roland Hollós accepts the primary-supervisor role, with weekly technical sessions through the modelling-intensive work packages and the supervision routine of the governance record.
Prof. András Jung accepts the co-supervisor role, carrying the hyperspectral/UAV/EO harmonisation strand as a substantive methodological role.

A six-month non-academic placement at AgroVIR provides operational model evaluation, agricultural-software requirements engineering, interoperability assessment, user-centred decision support and exploitation planning that the academic host cannot provide alone, with AgroVIR also consulted from the start of the action.

The M25-M30 placement is conducted mainly through remote collaboration with monthly face-to-face technical meetings for review, feedback and progress assessment. The fellow does not require direct access to AgroVIR's proprietary software, customer databases, office infrastructure or computing equipment; AgroVIR provides the information and data extracts required for interoperability testing in protected form (coded or anonymised field identifiers, e.g. 'Field X'). The fellow works with the AgroVIR product development team responsible for the FMIS platform.

A teaching/knowledge-transfer route via short guest lectures and seminars at MATE and the Agricultural University of Plovdiv transfers the fellow's approximately five years of university teaching (2015-2020) into the new discipline.
At least two high-quality peer-reviewed publications are targeted, with a possible third methods/application paper.

The resulting end-to-end profile is relevant to universities, European research organisations, precision-agriculture and irrigation-technology companies, Earth-observation/geospatial organisations, crop-phenotyping groups and FMIS providers.

The measures deliver the call's expected outcomes and impacts EO-01/EI-01 (increased research and transferable skills leading to improved employability inside and beyond academia), EO-02 (new mind-sets through international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary experience) and EI-02 (inter-sectoral knowledge transfer and expanded career opportunities).
